Architecture differences are useful only with their applicable targets, instruction variants, and evidence. These references keep those conditions next to the conclusions, with diagrams for the mappings and data paths that benefit from a visual explanation.

::: {.reading-guide}
**Choose your starting point.** Read an architecture comparison for hardware behavior, or a compiler article for LLVM dependency handling. The compiler articles introduce their own targets and operands; you can read them independently.
:::

## CDNA: architecture and LLVM

### Hardware differences

[**CDNA 3 and CDNA 4**](../cdna-architecture-compare/index.qmd) compares `gfx942` and `gfx950`, with particular attention to MFMA shapes, FNUZ versus OCP FP8, LDS resources, data movement, and synchronization.

- [Quick comparison](../cdna-architecture-compare/index.qmd#overview)
- [MFMA lane and register layouts](../cdna-architecture-compare/index.qmd#layout)
- [Memory paths and copy stride](../cdna-architecture-compare/index.qmd#memory)
- [Evidence status and limits](../cdna-architecture-compare/index.qmd#unconfirmed)
- [Migration priorities](../cdna-architecture-compare/index.qmd#migration-priorities)

### LLVM handling

[**LLVM on CDNA: MFMA dependencies and waits**](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd) covers target interfaces, physical register overlap, wait-state accounting, memory readiness and developer checks.

- [Findings and scope](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#compiler-behavior)
- [Shared FP16 dependency cases](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#mfma-compiler-cases)
:::

## Research scope

This topic covers AMD's RDNA and CDNA architectures. The two families have separate target scopes and evidence. Shared presentation does not imply shared hardware behavior.

Each document distinguishes ISA requirements, compiler behavior at a pinned revision, and properties confirmed only at the presentation level. Source review is separate from compilation, GPU execution, and performance validation.
